title: Thomas Fossey's notebook of veterinary recipes, 1710-1716 (Beinecke GEN MSS VOL 855): nine letters written as digits, read by Harumi-Matsuba

steps.what: Claude, directed by the contributor, transcribed the 38 images that carry cipher digits (36 distinct leaves, 625 lines) from the public IIIF images; the digit 9 and the letter g, 1 and the long s, 0 and d were separated at full resolution.
Digits sit inside otherwise ordinary English, only 1 to 9 occur and never 0, so they stand for letters; nine letters are replaced and the substitution is applied inconsistently.

The plain heading on image 18 ("for a blow in a horses eye to eat of ye Cell") is written again in cipher on image 19 ("f49 a b6455 38 a h49s2s ey2"), which fixes seven values; "18d" = and and "C9217" = Cream fix a and m.

1,000 shuffled keys against the real one: none reached it (real 96.8% of symbols in words that make sense, best shuffle 55.9%); no calibration exists (no contemporary decipherment, no printed edition).

Independent second readings from the images alone, with no key and no sight of the first reading: Claude Sonnet agrees with 90.2% to 90.7% of the decoded characters over all 36 images and OpenAI Codex with 91.3%; image 70, in two columns, first agreed 66.7% and 87.5% to 91.7% once a column rule was added.
The contributor searched the ledger, Tomokiyo's unsolved list, Cryptoole and GitHub: only the ledger entry of 28 Oct 2026 that names the method; no reading.

Project check: the key applied to the transcription gives the reading on 547 of 553 lines (the other six are comment lines); 55.4% of the 1,107 tokens with a digit decode to words written in clear elsewhere in the notebook, against at most 22.0% for 1,000 shuffled keys (VERIFICATION.md). No image compared.

validation.notes: The statistical test needs an English letter model (lang/, en-modern), whose corpus cannot be fetched from this environment (Gutenberg returns 403); it would also separate keys poorly when only nine letters of the text are replaced. The contributor's 1,000-shuffle control and a within-notebook vocabulary test against 1,000 shuffled keys were used instead (VERIFICATION.md).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was read from plaintext standing beside the cipher in the same notebook: a plain heading on image 18 repeated in cipher on image 19, and the words "and" and "Cream" on the next lines.

credits.note: key, transcription and reading of the Fossey notebook; issue #204; repository Harumi-Matsuba/fossey1710-public, CC BY 4.0

gaps.item: drug names, disease names and personal names whose spelling is not settled (131 symbols, 31 forms) and the 13 places where 9 and g are written alike
gaps.detail: the spellings are the writer's own and no reference text fixes them; the list is in contributor_open.md and open_tokens.tsv

gaps.item: lines hidden under pasted slips (images 25 to 34) and struck-through lines
gaps.detail: only the original can settle them; they are not visible in any image

gaps.item: a human check of the transcription against the Beinecke images, including the 9-or-g and 1-or-long-s places
gaps.detail: collections.library.yale.edu is not reachable from the project

outcome.notes: Key, transcription and reading by Harumi-Matsuba, with Claude and independent second readings by three models; checked by the project against the files and a within-notebook control, not against the images. No human has checked the transcription.
outcome.fraction_read_source: The contributor's count over the transcription: 3,332 of 3,492 cipher symbols (95.4%) fall in words that make sense without resolving the 13 places where 9 and g are written alike in favour of the reading that makes a word; with that step 3,359 of 3,490 (96.2%). 131 symbols stay open.

texts.label: Thomas Fossey's notebook of veterinary recipes, 1710-1716 (36 images with cipher)
texts.summary: Remedies for horses, cows and dogs, drinks, powders and a recipe for small beer, with drug names such as Crocus Metallorum and Diapente: 'a medicne for the Bite of a mad Dog', 'Six bushel of malt will Breuu four hogshead of Small Beer', 'beat it into uery fine pouder'.

reading_review.note: Read the decoded lines as English: recipes in the writer's own spelling form coherent clauses (for a blouu in a horses eye, fresh Cream and Bolarmery beat fine); drug and personal names stay open and the lines are short, so the review is of sense, not of grammar.

prior.where: The ledger entry of 28 Oct 2026 records the method ("vowels replaced by digits, trivially readable") but no key or reading; the contributor found no reading in the ledger, Tomokiyo, Cryptoole or on GitHub (1 Nov 2026).

human: Harumi-Matsuba directed the work and the checks (issue #204, repository Harumi-Matsuba/fossey1710-public); Claude did the transcription, the key, the control and the write-up, and three models of two families made independent second readings. No human has checked the transcription against the images.
